build.reason: The supplied recipe compiles this entry with an encoding definition and library headers, then links it against static Expat; the old setter remains declared in the changed source.

input.reason: The entry supplies fuzzer bytes and their size to parsing after the INT_MAX guard; finite valid XML input can reach the initialized parser's parse path.

lifecycle.reason: The entry creates two roots, conditionally resets parsers, creates children from a live parent, frees nonnull children, and finally frees the parent. Child reset is safely rejected by the source.

control_flow.reason: ParseOneInput sets the old salt before XML_Parse. For a nonzero derived salt, the setter marks the root key as set, so startParsing skips 16-byte generation and hashing uses a key with an upper zero word.

accepted.requirement: Parser hashing on the target's parse and external-entity surface must be able to use a full 16-byte salt from a supported high-quality source, through XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes before parsing or Expat's automatic generation.
accepted.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput creates root parsers and calls ParseOneInput; that helper computes an unsigned-long SipHash value from the bytes, calls XML_SetHashSalt, then calls XML_Parse. The entry later creates and parses child parsers.
accepted.failure_condition: For finite valid XML input with a nonzero derived SipHash value, XML_SetHashSalt writes zero to the upper key word, writes the value to the lower word, and sets the salt flag. XML_Parse then skips automatic salt generation. Internal hashing copies that limited key.
accepted.alternative_paths: The namespace root runs the same helper. Child parsers inherit the parent's salt and flag, then run the same helper; they do not invoke XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes. A zero derived salt can permit automatic generation, but does not provide the required full-salt route for nonzero-salt inputs or exercise explicit 16-byte configuration.

source_evidence.quote:
#47 #1183  CVE-2026-41080 -- The existing hash flooding protection
                    (based on SipHash) only used 4 to 8 bytes of entropy for
                    a salt, when 16 bytes of salt are supported by the
                    implementation of SipHash used by Expat. Now full 16 bytes
                    of entropy are used to improve protection against hash
                    flooding attacks.
                      Existing API function XML_SetHashSalt is now deprecated
                    because of its limitations, and its use should be
                    considered a vulnerability. Please either use the new API
                    function XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes (with known-high-quality
                    entropy input only!) instead, or leave the derivation of
                    a 16-bytes hash salt from high quality entropy to Expat's
                    internal machinery (by *not* calling either of the two
                    XML_SetHashSalt* functions).
